Subject: Clarify cookie consent & telemetry for Marketing Analytics

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — Acme is excited about the potential fit. Our privacy and security team has a few follow-ups specifically about tracking on the Redwood Console and public website, and about telemetry collected by the SDKs that power marketing analytics. High-level questions:

- What categories of cookies does Redwood set on the Console and public docs site (necessary, preferences, marketing/analytics)?
- Do you load any third-party pixels or marketing scripts by default?
- For telemetry: do you collect raw request payloads (e.g., prompt text) or only aggregated metrics? How long is any raw data retained?
- We need your current DPA and a list of subprocessors for vendor review.

Attached is our short questionnaire for vendors (acme_tmpl_questionnaire.xlsx). Can you point us to the DPA and subprocessor roster, and also let us know how users can opt out of marketing analytics?

Would prefer a short call if that is easier — happy to include our compliance lead (dp-compliance@acme-marketing.com).

Best,
Elena
Director, Product Data & Privacy
Acme Marketing, Inc.

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the short answers below and attached the DPA + current subprocessor roster for your legal team to review. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync with you and dp-compliance; propose Tues 3/18 at 10am PT — does that work?

Quick answers (high level):
- Cookies: Console uses necessary/session cookies and a small preference cookie for UI state; our public docs site sets a first-party analytics cookie (non-identifying) and an optional marketing cookie that is only enabled if a visitor consents to marketing analytics via the consent banner.
- Third-party pixels: By default we do not inject third-party marketing pixels on customer workspaces or console. Our docs site can load CDN-hosted analytics (first-party) and an opt-in Beaconly script for aggregated marketing metrics — Beaconly is a subprocessor (see roster).
- Telemetry & prompts: For hosted customers, telemetry includes performance metrics, error traces, and optional usage logs. We do not surface raw prompts to analytics pipelines by default; raw prompt retention is configurable by account and is typically disabled for marketing analytics. Default retention for hosted telemetry is 30 days unless extended by an enterprise agreement.
- Opt-out: end users can opt out of marketing analytics on the public site via the banner; for Console telemetry customers can opt out or request reduced retention via the Console privacy settings or by contacting support.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf, subprocessors_202503.csv

Next steps: confirm call time and we'll have Monica (CS) walk through telemetry controls and Markus (legal) on the DPA specifics.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — Monica from Customer Success here; closing the loop with more detail so your privacy folks have precise language they can copy into their assessment. I'm pasting bullets you can include in procurement notes.

- Cookie ownership: the marketing cookie is set as a first-party cookie on the public docs domain when a visitor explicitly consents to marketing analytics. Beaconly's script can be loaded only after consent; Beaconly receives hashed identifiers (no plaintext PII) and only aggregated event counts for marketing reports. We consider Beaconly a subprocessor; relevant contract stub attached (subprocessor_beaconly_contract_stub.pdf).

- Raw prompts / usage logs: Redwood does not forward raw prompt text to marketing analytics pipelines by default. For hosted customers, raw prompts may be retained in the request logs for debugging for a configurable window (default 30 days). Enterprise customers can:
  * disable prompt retention entirely, or
  * enable shorter retention windows, or
  * request on-prem / Dedicated deployment where data does not leave their VPC.
  There is a per-account export and deletion API we provide (see Console > Data Controls) and we can assist procurement with API endpoints for audit evidence.

- Cross-border transfers: for EU-origin data we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) with any US-based subprocessors and maintain transfer impact assessments. Customers with specific data residency requirements can use Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment to keep data in-region.

- Opt-out and consent flow: visitors who opt out via the consent banner will not load marketing scripts; the Console privacy settings allow company admins to toggle telemetry collection and set retention windows.

If you'd like, Markus can confirm the exact DPA clause numbers; Stephanie and I can join your procurement/counsel call. Proposed call: Tue 2025-03-18 10:00 PT (we'll include a brief demo of the Data Controls page).

Thanks,
